def test(page):
    # Precondition: Markor editor chrome with the "atlas" note title is shown.
    page.expect_image("initial-editor", region=[0, 128, 330, 212],
                      threshold=0.1, max_diff_pixels=20, precondition=True)

    # Focus the editor body and type the note text.
    page.click(360, 600)
    page.type_text("Bring the blue notebook.")

    # Save explicitly via the toolbar save icon.
    page.click(569, 170)

    # Close and reopen the application.
    page.reload()

    # Behavioral check: the saved text is visible after reopening.
    page.expect_image("saved-reopened", region=[0, 215, 720, 330],
                      threshold=0.1, max_diff_pixels=10,
                      observation_window_ms=2000)

I saved the test to `/workspace/output/test.py`. I haven't run it, because there is no way to execute it here. I did walk through the same steps by hand in the live app, and the text was still in the note after the app closed and reopened.

**What the test does, in order:**
1. **Setup check:** confirms the editor's title bar showing "atlas" matches a screenshot I saved (`initial-editor`) before any changes.
2. Taps the empty note and types `Bring the blue notebook.`
3. Taps the save icon in the toolbar (at 569, 170).
4. Closes and reopens the app.
5. **Main check:** compares the note's text area (pixels from y 215 to 330) against a screenshot I saved after reopening (`saved-reopened`). It allows up to 10 differing pixels and watches for 2 seconds.

**Risk:** the blinking text cursor ends up right after the period when the note reopens. I didn't mask it out, because a mask there could hide a missing or extra character. The test relies on catching at least one frame within the 2 seconds where the cursor is hidden. My reference screenshot is one such frame. If the cursor ever stays visible for the whole window, the main check could fail even when the note is correct.
